## Why it works

Viewers praise its clarity and the payoff method. "I vowed not to use Wago. Until I used some!!! Changed my life" (231 likes); "Lots of this sort on YouTube, the difference is the clarity of the explanations, thank you." (69 likes); "That's what I prefer, short explanations all necessary info included without ballast." (30 likes). Two of the most-liked comments are corrections or additions from tradespeople: "2.5mm twin and earth only has a 1.5mm earth so you should use a red crimp on the cpc conductor" (140 likes) and "When showing the use of either crimp- or in-line pushfit connectors, it would be helpful also to show their removal" (98 likes). A viewer acted on it: "I have to re wire my garage and had never heard of the inline splice. I only watched this out of curiosity but I am so happy I did. This is going to save me hours of work" (3 likes). The pace is quick (about 194 words a minute), the hard way comes first so the easy way feels like a gift ("how much easier and quicker was that" (5:21)), and the verdict is said as a personal switch ("since using these I haven't gone back to the crimps" (5:26)). Compared with E09's opening: E09 puts the viewer in the job and states the rule; this one states the goal and holds back the better method, which costs it a tease and an announcement we can't use, but the old-way-then-new-way order is a shape we can.
